origin: Boutsen VDS emerged from the fusion of two distinct Belgian motorsport entities: the Boutsen family's established racing pedigree and the VDS Racing Adventures program. Thierry Boutsen, a seasoned Formula 1 driver with a proven track record, sought to nurture young talent and keep the Boutsen name synonymous with racing excellence. Simultaneously, VDS Racing Adventures, a wealthy Belgian motorsport enthusiast group, aimed to provide aspiring drivers with high-quality machinery and expert coaching. The partnership formed in the late 2000s, with the initial focus on GT racing and endurance events, leveraging the Boutsen name for sponsorship opportunities and VDS's financial backing to acquire competitive equipment. A pivotal moment came early when a young driver, under their tutelage, secured a podium finish at the Spa 24 Hours, instantly validating the team's approach.
philosophy: Boutsen VDS operates on the principle of blending experience with youthful ambition. Their approach to car development is iterative, relying heavily on driver feedback and data analysis, rather than radical overhauls. The team culture emphasizes a family atmosphere, fostering open communication and mutual respect between drivers, engineers, and mechanics. While aiming for victory, the team prioritizes driver development and creating a sustainable racing program.
achievements: Podium finish at the Spa 24 Hours (2010)
Multiple class victories in the Blancpain Endurance Series
Champion Team in the Belgian GT Championship (2012)
Nurtured several drivers who progressed to professional racing careers

teamPrincipal.name: Olivia Boutsen
teamPrincipal.background: Olivia, daughter of Thierry Boutsen, took over the team principal role after his semi-retirement. She brings a modern, data-driven approach to team management, while maintaining the family's commitment to driver development.

keyFigures.name: Marc Duez
keyFigures.description: A veteran Belgian racing driver, Marc Duez brings decades of experience and track knowledge to Boutsen VDS. He oversees the team's racing operations and driver coaching programs.

keyFigures.name: Jean-Michel Baise
keyFigures.description: Jean-Michel is responsible for the technical direction of the team and car development. He has a keen eye for detail and a pragmatic approach to problem-solving.

headquarters: The team is based near Nivelles, Belgium, with a modest workshop facility. While the facilities are not cutting-edge, they are well-maintained and equipped for basic race preparation and maintenance.
fanBase: Boutsen VDS attracts a loyal following of Belgian motorsport enthusiasts, drawn to the team's commitment to nurturing local talent and their consistent presence in national and international GT racing. Their fans appreciate the team's approachable nature and dedication to the sport.
